Significance brackets indicate days where EXP and OBS occupancy differ significantly (two-sided t-tests or Brunner-Munzel tests, FDR-corrected across all days; D1: Brunner-Munzel, BM = 2.808, p = 0.0305*; D2: Brunner-Munzel, BM = 4.289, p = 0.0059**; D3: t-test, t(17) = −2.937, p = 0.0246*; D4: Brunner-Munzel, BM = 4.216, p = 0.0059**; D5: t-test, t(17) = −2.666, p = 0.0305*; D6: Brunner-Munzel, BM = 2.308, p = 0.0393*; D7: t-test, t(17) = −2.499, p = 0.0307*; D8: t-test, t(17) = −1.745, p = 0.0991, n.s.). d, Occupancy of attacks during day 1, day 8, and the hard fight for EXP animals (n = 10 paired animals; box plots as in b, with lines connecting the same animal across the three timepoints). Omnibus comparison via Friedman test (F = 1.400, p = 0.4966, n.s.) e, Occupancy (left) and latency (right) of fleeing events during the hard fight by EXP (orange, N = 10), OBS (magenta, N = 9), and NON (grey, N = 8) animals. Occupancy: omnibus Kruskal-Wallis, H = 7.652, p = 0.0218; post-hoc two-sided Brunner-Munzel tests, FDR-corrected across comparisons: EXP vs. OBS (BM = 1.207, p = 0.2440, n.s.), EXP vs. NON (BM = 3.461, p = 0.0100*), OBS vs. NON (BM = 2.150, p = 0.0742, n.s.). Latency: omnibus Kruskal-Wallis, H = 1.662, p = 0.4356, n.s. Box plots as in b. f, Probability distribution of frames containing attacks found in each UMAP cluster during the hard fight. Clusters 2, 3, and 4 contain the highest proportion of attack frames, consistent with their designation as conflict clusters. g, Leave-one-session-out cross-validation balanced accuracy of group ID (EXP, OBS, NON) predictions using UMAP cluster occupancy as the classification feature, evaluated against a null distribution generated by a permutation test (1,000 permutations, group labels shuffled independently per session, one-sided; p = 0.0010***). h, Same as g but using pairwise transition probabilities between UMAP clusters as the classification feature (permutation test as in g; p = 0.0020**). i, Top: Same as g but using cluster persistence (average consecutive bout duration, seconds) as the classification feature (permutation test as in g; p = 0.0010***). Bottom: Persistence of all 13 behaviour clusters across groups (EXP N = 10, OBS N = 9, NON N = 8) during the hard fight (box plots as in b; one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test pending normality, post-hoc two-sided t-tests or Brunner-Munzel tests, FDR-corrected; full statistics in Table S1). j, Subset of averaged SLEAP-derived features across groups during the hard fight (EXP N = 10, OBS N = 9, NON N = 8; box plots as in b). Features shown: resident-intruder centroid distance, resident centroid speed, resident-intruder body overlap, intruder centroid speed. Full statistics in Table S1. For all comparisons, *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001.

a, Schematic and mathematical descriptions of all SLEAP-derived features used for behavioural segmentation, organized by category. Distance features capture inter-animal proximity and approach dynamics. The bounding box category includes intersection over union (IoU), computed via Shapely polygon operations, which measures the degree of physical overlap between animal bounding boxes. Social orientation features capture the directed facing angle of each animal relative to the other. Postural features include within-mouse head angle (centroid–neck–head angle, indexing sniffing posture and body curvature) and within-mouse body length (tailbase-to-head distance, indexing body elongation). Speed features are computed as the rate of change (ROC) of position over a 4-frame window (100 ms), including within-mouse translational (centroid) speed and head-specific speed for both resident and intruder, as well as a summed speed feature aggregating across temporal lags spanning ±2 s. b, Unsupervised behaviour states resulting from watershed segmentation of the UMAP embedding, with descriptions organized according to the unsupervised hierarchical clustering results depicted in Fig. 1m, which segregates behavioural states into three discrete categories: conflict and aggression-preparatory states (red; clusters 1–4), investigative or social engagement states (gold; clusters 5, 7–9), and disengaged or avoidant states (green; clusters 6, 10–13). The behavioural content of each cluster is ascertained via a combination of manual curation of video frames across multiple sessions and animals and feature coding as shown in (c). c, Feature maps of all 13 behavioural clusters across all recorded SLEAP-derived behaviour features, including resident and intruder centroid speed, resident and intruder head speed, resident-intruder centroid distance, resident head to intruder head distance, resident head to intruder tailbase distance, intruder head to resident tailbase distance, resident-intruder orientation, intruder-resident orientation, resident-intruder body overlap (IoU), resident body length, intruder body length, resident body orientation, and intruder body orientation. Each map depicts the mean z-scored feature value projected onto the UMAP behaviour space, averaged across animals and sessions. d, Representative video frames depicting examples of each behavioural cluster, organized according to the same hierarchical grouping as in (b). Conflict states (clusters 1–4): mutual conflict, resident aggression, aggression preparation 1, aggression preparation 2. Investigative states (clusters 5, 7–9): huddled investigation, non-specific/orofacial investigation, mutual investigation, mutually facing investigation. Disengaged/avoidant states (clusters 6, 10, 11, 13): intruder disengages, intruder approaches/investigates, avoidance with resident movement 1, avoidance with resident movement 2, avoidance with resident scrunch/groom. Resident animals are indicated by cyan markers and intruder animals by red markers.

a, Schematic depicting the timeline of exposure training. In contrast to OBS animals, nonsocial exposure (XPO, N = 5) animals observed non-aggressive male cagemates for 8 days, and on day 9 were pitted against three rounds of CD1 aggressors. b, Leave-one-session-out cross-validation balanced accuracy of group ID (OBS vs. XPO) predictions using occupancy of UMAP clusters (left), persistence (mean length of cluster bouts, middle), and pairwise cluster transition probabilities (right) as classification features. For each metric, test balanced accuracy was evaluated against a null distribution generated by a permutation test (1,000 permutations, group labels shuffled independently per session, one-sided; occupancy, p = 0.0010***; persistence, p = 0.0010***; transitions, p = 0.0010***). c, Occupancy of a subset of behaviour clusters for OBS (N = 9) and XPO (N = 5) animals during the hard fight: clusters 2 and 4 (conflict), 5 and 7 (investigative), and 6 and 10 (asocial) — two representative clusters per behavioural category, selected a priori based on the category structure established in Fig. 1. Box plots: line represents median; box, 25th–75th percentile; whiskers, min/max within 1.5x IQR; points overlaid; individual points overlaid. Group differences evaluated via two-sided t-tests or Brunner-Munzel tests where no directional hypothesis existed, and one-sided tests where an a priori direction was established by the corresponding effect in Fig. 1: clusters 2, 4, 5, 7 tested one-sided (OBS > XPO) followed by FDR correction; clusters 6, 10 tested one-sided (OBS < XPO) followed by FDR correction. Full statistics in Table S1. d, Aggregate transition weights between behaviour-category clusters (as in Fig. 1o), OBS versus XPO, hard fight, for a subset of transitions of a priori interest from Fig. 1: conflict→conflict, conflict→investigation and asocial→investigation (one-sided, OBS > XPO); investigation→investigation and investigation→asocial (two-sided); and asocial→asocial (one-sided, OBS < XPO). N and box plots as in c. Tests: one-sided t-tests or Brunner-Munzel tests, followed by FDR corrections across comparisons in the same family of origin behaviours. Full statistics in Table S1. e, Classification strategy for determining EXP-like or NON-like behavioural tendency of OBS versus XPO animals during the hard fight. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier is trained on EXP and NON behaviour using cluster occupancy, persistence, or pairwise transition probabilities as separate feature sets. Each classifier is then applied to OBS and XPO animals, with individuals classified as EXP-like or NON-like based on the classifier output. f, Left: Distribution of P(classified as EXP) for OBS (N = 9, magenta) versus XPO (N = 5, cyan) animals, using cluster occupancy as the classifier feature (two-sided Brunner-Munzel test, BM = −2.956, p = 0.0193*). Box plots as in c. Middle: as in left, using cluster persistence (BM = −3.164, p = 0.0083**). Right: as in left, using pairwise transition probabilities (BM = −2.563, p = 0.0281*). For all comparisons, *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001.

a, Representative GCaMP6f (green) or JRCaMP2b (red) expression across all 12 recorded brain areas. Scale bars 500 μm. Representative of fibre placement confirmed via histology in the majority of subjects per region (range: 8/12–12/12 for EXP; 9/9 for OBS; 8/8 for NON, across all regions); full per-region counts in b. b, Accepted fibre placements for every experimental subject across all 12 recorded brain areas. Coronal schematics are adapted from the Allen Brain Atlas51. Fraction of subjects per group with histologically confirmed placement, by region (EXP / OBS / NON): PrL, 11/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; vLS, 12/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; POA, 11/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; BNST, 10/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; AH, 10/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; MeA, 11/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; VMH, 12/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; PAG, 8/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; PMv, 9/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; LHb (excitatory only), 9/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; PA, 9/12 / 9/9 / 8/8; NAc (dopamine), 11/12 / 9/9 / 8/8.

a, Model architecture. Input clips of 20 frames (0.5 s) are passed through stochastic augmentations during training, followed by four 3D convolutional attention blocks, each consisting of a 3D convolution, batch normalization, max pooling, and a spatial attention module. The encoder output is pooled into a 512-dimensional feature vector and passed to a three-layer MLP classifier producing softmax probabilities over seven behavioural classes. The seven output classes are merged into four behaviour categories: attention (attention), self-directed (grooming, scratching), idle (still), and exploratory (investigate, rearing, turning). Fine-grained class colours are shown within each category in the legend. b, Spatial attention maps from the first three encoder blocks for four behavioural classes selected to span distinct postures (rearing, scratching, turning, attention). Each row shows a single representative frame from one held-out clip. Maps from the fourth block are omitted due to coarse spatial resolution. Within each panel, attention values are min-max normalized; brighter colours indicate higher attention weight. c, Row-normalized confusion matrix for the four behaviour categories, averaged across the 5 cross-validation folds. Cell values give the mean percentage of ground-truth samples assigned to each predicted category ± SD across folds. d, Example behavioural time series from three training sessions across the first 5 min of observation. Coloured bars indicate the classifier assigned behavioural category at each frame: attention (blue), self-directed (yellow), idle (grey), and exploratory (orange). Dark red dots mark demonstrator attack labels from an independent attack behaviour classifier (see Supervised behaviour classification in Methods). e, Behaviour category occupancy of OBS animals (N = 9 mice) during training period. f, Daily behaviour category occupancy for OBS (top, N = 9 mice) and XPO (bottom, N = 5 mice) animals across the training period. Attention proportion was modelled separately per condition by a linear mixed-effects model with day as a continuous fixed effect and a random intercept per mouse (occupancy ~ day + (1 | mouse), REML); significance is the two-sided Wald z-test on the day coefficient (OBS, β = 0.018 occupancy/ day, p = 0.002**; XPO, β = 0.011, p = 0.229, n.s.). Error bars, ±SEM across mice. g, Behaviour category occupancy (fraction of time occupied relative to total session length) compared between OBS (magenta, N = 9) and XPO (cyan, N = 5) animals during the training period. From left to right: attention occupancy (two-sided independent samples t-test: t(12) = 2.26, p = 0.044*), self-directed occupancy (two-sided independent samples t-test: t(12) = 0.166, p = 0.8713, n.s.), idle occupancy (two-sided Brunner-Munzel test: BM = 1.884, p = 0.0852 n.s.), exploratory occupancy (two-sided independent samples t-test: t(12) = −2.47, p = 0.0294). Box plots: line represents median; box, 25th–75th percentile; whiskers, min/max within 1.5x IQR; individual animal points overlaid h, Entropy (bits) of behaviour category occupancy distributions for OBS and XPO animals, computed as Shannon entropy across the four merged behavioural categories (two-sided independent samples t-test: t(12) = 2.248, p = 0.062 n.s.). Box plot and N as in g. i, Behaviour occupancy of OBS animals (N = 9) across attack relative time windows compared to a matched per-animal baseline. Windows: before attack onset (−25 to 0%), attack onset (0 to 25%), attack middle (25 to 75%), attack end (75 to 100%), and after attack offset (100 to 125%); baseline is mean behaviour occupancy across all training days. Error bars, ±SEM. Asterisks indicate significant deviation from baseline (two-sided paired t-tests with FDR correction, for full statistics see Table S1). j, Left: Average difference in behaviour category occupancy between attack and control periods across OBS animals (N = 9). Control segments were randomly drawn from non-attack frames across 50 independent trials, matched in total duration to attack segments (two-sided paired t-tests with FDR correction; attention: 0.0063**. Self-directed: 0.0083**). Right: Average mean latency to onset for each behavioural state during attack versus control periods across OBS animals (N = 9). Error bars, ±SEM across trials (two-sided paired t-tests with FDR correction; n.s). k, Average behaviour category occupancy at attack onset, before vs. after time-shifting across OBS animals (N = 9). A window of 2 s around attack onset is used for this analysis. After time-shifting, there is a significant increase in attention (p = 0.0098**) and decrease in idle (p = 0.0098**), and exploratory behaviours (p = 0.0372*) (two-sided paired t-tests with FDR correction). Error bars, ±SEM. l, Decoding performance (F1 score) for behaviour category labels in OBS animals (N = 9), comparing all recorded regions combined (filled bars), the best single region (outlined bars), and permutation-based chance (grey bars). The best single region was selected independently for each mouse and behaviour as the region yielding the highest mean F1 across cross-validation repeats. Error bars indicate ± SEM; dots show individual mice. Upper brackets indicate all regions vs. chance paired comparisons, lower brackets indicate all regions vs. best single region paired comparisons. P-values of two-sided paired t-tests with FDR correction are reported as (all vs. chance, all vs. best single region): attention (p = 9.54e-9***, p = 7.65e-4***); self-directed (p = 1.48e-6***, p = 1.87e-6***); idle (p = 3.28e-4***, p = 2.02e-4***); exploratory (p = 6.01e-7***, p = 8.89e-6***). m, Average SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values of signals’ contribution to decoding performance across OBS animals (N = 9), split by observer behaviour category. Error bars, ±SEM. For all comparisons, *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001.

a, Overview schematic of the time-shifting process. Top left: A tensor of SBN activity is constructed with dimensions trial × attack window × neural population. Top middle: The model learns a population-specific activity template from the components of each recorded population. Bottom middle: The model learns the likely timing of activity on a trial-by-trial basis, yielding a distribution of per-trial time shifts ranging from −2 s to +2 s. Trials shifted in the negative direction are depicted in dark green and trials shifted in the positive direction in light green; unshifted trials are shown in grey-green. A negative skew in shift distribution (shifts <0) is evaluated via a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test (N = 1,115 trials, W = 258,136.5, p = 3.98 × 10−7***). Top right: The end result of the pipeline proceeds from unshifted signals through time-shifted alignment to attention-state filtering (ATTN+ versus ATTN−). b, Peri-event time histograms of excitatory (top) and inhibitory (bottom) SBN populations and valence areas for OBS animals, comparing time-shifted, attention-filtered (magenta) versus unshifted, attention-filtered (blue) attack-aligned signals (z-ΔF/F, mean, shaded area ± SEM). Shifted and unshifted signals are shown for each recorded region across the full network. For each population, post-attack mean activity (baseline-corrected) is compared against zero using two-sided one-sample t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests pending normality, with FDR correction across all regions. For full statistics, including N per population, see Table S1. For all comparisons, *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001. c, To validate that time-shifting of neural signals does not spuriously generate neural activity, three control conditions were devised in which the same time-shifting model was applied to OBS animals. In the first condition, the model was applied to neural signals during randomly resampled behavioural events generated by a Markov chain trained to reproduce attack patterns (frequency and duration) at random time points not overlapping with real aggression (“synthetic,” light blue). In the second condition, the model was applied to neural signals during high resident velocity events unrelated to aggression (“speed,” dark blue-green). In the third condition, the model was applied to NON animal neural signals during random indices derived from real attack timepoints in OBS animals (“yoked,” grey). d, Peri-event time histograms (z-ΔF/F) of SBN and valence system activity for synthetic (left) and speed (right) control conditions (mean, shaded area ± SEM). Neural signals from each control condition are overlaid on OBS signals from Fig. 2j.

a, Illustration of the half-decay time metric applied to representative EXP (left) and OBS (right) subjects for VMHvl excitatory and inhibitory populations. Each trace shows the baseline-corrected, attack-aligned mean z-ΔF/F signal. The peak value (red dot) is identified within the post-attack window and the half-decay time t½ (yellow dot) is defined as the time from peak to the point at which the signal first returns to 50% of its peak value, estimated with sub-frame precision via linear interpolation. The baseline noise floor (2 × baseline SD) is used as a minimum threshold for valid peak detection. b, Half-decay time t½ (s) of attack-aligned calcium signals across all recorded excitatory (green) and inhibitory (blue) SBN populations, for EXP (orange) and OBS (magenta) animals during the training period. Box plots: line represents median; box, 25th–75th percentile; whiskers, min/max within 1.5x IQR; individual animal points overlaid. Regions are ordered with excitatory populations first, followed by inhibitory populations. For each region, EXP versus OBS comparisons are performed using two-sided independent samples t-tests or Brunner-Munzel tests pending normality, with FDR correction across all populations. For detailed statistics, see Table S1. c, Within-group comparison of half-decay time t½ between excitatory (light green) and inhibitory (light blue) populations for EXP animals, shown for each paired SBN region (VMHvl, PMv, AH, POA, MeA, PA, BNST, lPAG, vLS, PrL). Each point represents one animal; lines connect paired excitatory and inhibitory measurements from the same animal. Significance brackets indicate regions where excitatory half-decay time is significantly shorter than inhibitory half-decay time (one-sided paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests pending normality, with FDR correction across all regions). For detailed statistics, see Table S1. d, As in c but for OBS animals. For all comparisons, *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001.

a, Average group-specific tuning curves (mean, shaded area +/− SEM) depicting the encoding of inter-animal proximity across hypothalamic and amygdala regions during the hard fight, shown as a function of binned proximity (close to far). Each tuning curve represents a set of GLM weights fit for each feature and each region independently, using a leave-one-animal-out cross-validation procedure, for EXP (orange), OBS (magenta), and NON (grey) animals. Boxed regions indicate representative neural populations selected for display. Highlighted areas in each curve denote the first five bins (blue) and last five bins (red) of each tuning curve, corresponding to low and high values of the encoded feature respectively. Tuning curves for which the cross-validated R² does not exceed zero are blurred to indicate poor model fit and low predictive power; region–feature combinations are only included in group comparisons if at least two groups show R² significantly greater than zero (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test). For full R² comparisons and pairwise group statistics, see Table S1. b, As in a but for resident self-speed (low to high). c, As in a but for CD1 aggressor speed (low to high).

a, Peri-event time histograms (z-ΔF/F) of inhibitory PMv, AH, MeA, and BNST populations, aligned to conflict bout onset (irrespective of attack direction) during the hard fight, for EXP (orange), OBS (magenta), and NON (grey) animals (mean ± SEM). b, Mean z-ΔF/F during the conflict period for each recorded population, excitatory populations and LHb (top row) and inhibitory populations and NAc DA (bottom row), EXP/OBS/NON. Individual animals shown as points; horizontal line indicates the group mean, error bar indicates +/− SEM. N per population in Table S1. Group comparisons: omnibus one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test pending normality, post-hoc two-sided t-tests or Brunner-Munzel tests, FDR-corrected within population; full statistics in Table S1. For all comparisons, *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001.

Schematic summarizing the relationship between inhibitory SBN ensemble activity and behavioural state across experimental groups. The x-axis represents the inhibitory ensemble state, indexed by population activity level and/or VMHvl coupling strength. The y-axis represents aggression preparedness, ranging from avoidant to aggressively prepared. NON animals, which lack social experience, occupy a high inhibitory ensemble / low preparedness state. OBS and EXP animals shift rightward and upward along both axes following observation and direct fighting experience respectively, reflecting reduced inhibitory tone and increased aggression preparedness. Reactivation of inhibition returns OBS animals toward the NON-like state, demonstrating that inhibitory ensemble activity is both necessary and sufficient to gate aggression preparedness in a novel aggression context.

#1430. How Spurs turned their season around: Fiery three-hour meeting before Man United clash, the star who has lit a spark in struggling side and why Rodrigo Bentancur's red card was a key moment

Published: 18:07 EDT, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 18:20 EDT, 6 November 2026

Choose your Tottenham turning point. The training break in Marbella perhaps. The first win of the season against Coventry, the return of James Maddison, or a rare and emotional victory at Chelsea, only second time in 36 years.

Roberto De Zerbi, the man who has turned the tanker on the pitch, goes instinctively to a heated team meeting before the Manchester United game. It lasted for three hours, from 8pm to 11pm in the team hotel in Manchester city centre.

De Zerbi detected more fire and passion in the meeting room that day and realised change was in the air. He enjoyed hearing home truths exchanged among teammates and between them and his staff members.

'In normal meetings you speak about tactics and mentality,' said De Zerbi. 'In that meeting there was something different. If you are honest in the meeting and you remove the mask and explain your weaknesses a teammate can help you in a difficult moment.

'I believe in people, in relationships, in connections. I don't believe in robots. I don't believe you can come here, put on the shirt and go on the pitch. I believe in the right atmosphere. I love it when I see my players come together to help each other, coming to the stadium even when not selected in the squad. It's crucial.

'Sometimes you can fight but fight for the good of the club not for yourself. Not egoist players but he team, before everything.'

Spurs have won their last three matches having turned the corner under Roberto De Zerbi

Manchester United was the first fixture after the last international break. Spurs were bottom of the Premier League.

They played well at Old Trafford without capitalising, then went behind and had Rodrigo Bentancur sent off for butting Luke Shaw before summoning a fight back, with Dominic Solanke heading in a late equaliser from a cross by Sandro Tonali, the £100million midfielder who finished the game playing at left back.

It provided a spark. Spurs won the next three.

The impact of Bentancur's ban was amplified by Lucas Bergvall's knee injury in the same game. Neither have played since, although Bentancur is available again at Leeds, and De Zerbi reflects positively on the Uruguayan's rush of blood.

'Very important,' said the Spurs boss. 'I don't know if without that red card the reaction would have been like this, but the reaction was good because sometimes we are afraid to show more passion.

'I like people to say Tottenham played well but I want people to say Tottenham played with passion. That they were strong and helped each other on the pitch. That they had hot blood inside. That they played for the club and the fans. My dream is to hear people talk like this.'

Without Bentancur and Bergvall, De Zerbi flexed into a 352 formation against Coventry. Maddison started his first game for nearly 18 months and Spurs won for the first time this season, then disappeared on secretive training break for four nights in Marbella.

They were back in a familiar 4231 shape against Chelsea with Mateus Fernandes starting for the first time since he had been hooked at half time against Aston Villa and criticised by De Zerbi.

Fernandes was the best player on the pitch and clicked with Tonali and the pair excelled again against Crystal Palace.

For all the best laid plans, some good things can happen by chance.

Rodrigo Bentancur's red card in the draw with Man United has proved a key moment for Spurs

Back in August, in the aftermath of a 2-0 defeat by Newcastle in the first home game of this season, Tonali stood near the dressing rooms in conversation with club owners Vivienne Lewis and her son-in-law Nick Beucher.

Tonali was disconsolate. The new Spurs regime had invested a club record fee to sign him at the behest of De Zerbi but he was sluggish, miles from his best and had just been given the runaround by Nico Gonzalez, the player bought to replace him for half the price.

His body language was apologetic, and the owners appeared keen to offer some words of encouragement as they bid farewells and took a lift to the corporate suites in the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Two months on, the Italian has hit his stride. He has been dominant in the last two games. Sharper in mind, more decisive and quicker across the ground. Reading play, breaking things down, covering the miles. He looks like an elite midfielder.

'To play well, Tonali has to run and to work on the pitch,' said De Zerbi before hinting at more to come from Fernandes. 'Mateus is showing 50-60 per cent of his potential,' said the Spurs boss.

For all the rhetoric about unity, the return of Maddison has reset the creativity levels. His presence lifted the crowd and had a similar effect on his teammates. Possession is more secure. His quality on the ball gives others time to organise and with him Spurs look a lot more like scoring a goal. Passes fizz around at a brisker tempo and he carries threat from around the fringes of the penalty box. The goal he swept into the top corner to open the scoring against Coventry was exquisite.

Sandro Tonali has become a vital player for De Zerbi after a mixed start to his Tottenham career

Mo Kudus is back and Dejan Kulusevski's return after so long lifted morale. Less obvious is the return of Dominic Solanke, a genuine centre forward who can operate with his back to goal and bring others into play. Solanke has helped the team gel even if his goal return remains disappointing and De Zerbi admits he and Omar Marmoush are suffering low confidence.

After being criticised for ignoring the club's academy talent, De Zerbi has tried to integrate Luca Williams-Barnett. He cannot talk about togetherness if he refuses to engage with one significant arm of the club. Williams-Barnett made his Premier League debut as a sub against Palace. De Zerbi claimed he thought about starting him at Chelsea and urged the 18-year-old attacking midfielder to learn from those around him.

'The young player has to remove all social media and stay focused on improvement,' said De Zerbi. 'They have to follow the older teammates with more experience and work hard. Expectation and hype is normal. He can become a top player and has to get used to strong pressure and high expectation.'

Win at Leeds on Saturday and Spurs will go into another international break in touch with the top five. It has been quite a turnaround and chief executive Vinai Venkatesham popped up on a podcast this week talking about ambitions to win the Premier League title.

'Great to hear,' said De Zerbi. 'The first thing for people in this club is to be ambitious but to be ambitious you have to show the right mentality every day, game by game because words are not enough.

'What Vinai, the Lewis family and Johan Lange are doing is something special. In the last two seasons you can see they are changing a lot of things in this club. For me as coach, my staff and the players, we have to show we have the self to stay in this club.

'With the right behaviour, the right mentality, to be angry every day and to make a result. This is the best thing to do from our side.'

#1429. Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

And City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a new team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This shows how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”

By Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland said. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the big stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig

“I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. “Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

Enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw

That is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

That is a big chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

Porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

#1428. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

#1427. Man United fans urge supporters to REFUSE to buy booze at Old Trafford as groups ramp up anti-Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe protests ahead of Sunday's clash with Aston Villa

Published: 04:44 EDT, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 04:49 EDT, 7 November 2026

Manchester United fan groups are calling for a booze boycott at Sunday’s game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as part of their protests against the club’s owners.

Supporters have revived the green and gold campaign against the Glazer family in recent weeks, with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe also in their sights.

During Tuesday’s Champions League win over Roma at Old Trafford, green and gold balloons were released from the Stretford End before kick-off and tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch in the 20th minute.

Now groups including Reclaim the Stretford End, The 1958, The Red Army, Manchester United Youth Supporters’ Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds are urging fans to hit the owners in the pocket by refusing to buy alcohol in the stadium at the Villa game.

Supporters have been asked to release balloons again when the teams come out before the match, but to respect the minute’s silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The joint organisers say they are protesting against the ownership, the plans to knock down Old Trafford and build a new 100,000-seater stadium next door, United’s debts of more than £1billion, and what they say is a decline in standards throughout the club and the disrespect being shown to match-going fans.

Manchester United supporter groups have urged fans to follow an alcohol boycott

Fan groups are ramping up protests against the Glazer family and co-owners INEOS

Details of the new protest have emerged after it was confirmed that three people were arrested for throwing tennis balls onto the pitch during the Roma game. The game had to be halted temporarily as the players helped to remove them.

Greater Manchester Police made a further eight arrests including four for assault, two for public order offences, one for fraud and one for possession of Class B drugs.

But the game passed off without the serious trouble that has marred previous meetings between United and Roma dating back to their first meeting in the quarter-final of the Champions League in April 2007 when Italian riot police were widely criticised for wading into English fans after they reacted to being pelted with missiles by Roma supporters.

United famously won the return leg 7-1 when police made 18 arrests after fans clashed outside Old Trafford.

#1426. Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome1. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors2, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR–Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal–fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

(a) Schematic diagram illustrating the preparation of subgenomic RNA-containing VLPs or empty VLPs with DogTag inserted into the envelope proteins. Plasmids encoding C-DTE2-E1, which contains an in-frame DogTag insertion between Gly1 and Leu2 of the E2 protein, and C-E2-DTE1, which contains an in-frame DogTag insertion between Asn213 and Gln214 of the E1 protein, were also expressed. Expi293F cells were utilized to produce large quantities of empty VLPs. (b) A series of SGR-VLPs encoding NanoLuc as a reporter were inoculated into Vero cells to assess infectivity. As a negative control, culture medium collected from BHK-SGR-NL cells expressing mCherry instead of CE2E1 was used. Infectivity was determined by measuring the relative activity of NanoLuc (n = 3 biologically independent cultures). (c) Western blot analysis to detect the E2 (left panel) or E1 (right panel) protein of SGR-VLPs. SGR-VLPs were incubated overnight at 4 °C in the presence or absence of DC-APEX2. SDS-PAGE samples were prepared by adding SGR-VLPs to SDS-PAGE sample buffer containing 2-mercaptoethanol and incubating at 95 °C for 5 min. Arrows indicate the original bands of viral proteins with an inserted DogTag, while arrowheads indicate those covalently bound to DC-APEX2. (d) Infectivity analysis of SGR-VLP mixed with PBS or DC-APEX2. SGR-VLPs were incubated overnight at 4 °C with PBS or DC-APEX2 and subsequently inoculated into Vero cells to analyze infectivity. As a negative control, culture medium collected from BHK-SGR-NL cells expressing mCherry instead of CE2E1 was used. Infectivity was determined by measuring the relative activity of NanoLuc (n = 4 biologically independent cultures). (e) Electron microscopic images of VLPs and APEX2-VLPs visualized by negative staining. (f) Following treatment of JAR4-SMS1KO22 cells under the indicated conditions, biotin-labeled proteins were detected by western blotting using HRP-conjugated streptavidin. (g) Fluorescence staining images of JAR4-SMS1KO22 cells treated with biotin labeling in the presence or absence of APEX2-VLP. RuV E1 protein, biotin, and nuclei are visualized in green, magenta, and blue, respectively. Images in left and upper right panels were obtained by confocal microscopy and are shown as z-stack projections. The boxed area in the left panel is magnified in the upper right panel. The cross-section obtained by cutting along the dotted line in the left panel is shown in the lower right panel. The plasma membranes stained with WGA are shown in gray in only the cross-section image. Data are mean ± s.d.
